ai.description: This lizard reaches 12–22 cm. It features a bronze-brown back with dark lateral stripes and orange-red flanks in breeding males. Key features include keeled scales and a distinct pale dorsolateral line.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Eutropis multifasciata* is the presence of three distinct, strongly keeled scales on the mid-dorsal region, unlike other similar skinks.
ai.habitat: The Common Mabuya inhabits moist, low-altitude tropical forests, gardens, and plantations, often found near leaf litter or debris in humid, vegetated environments.
ai.behavior: The Common Mabuya is a diurnal lizard that actively forages for insects on the forest floor and often basks on logs or rocks to regulate its body temperature.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis multifasciata* is ovoviviparous, producing clutches of 4–12 young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eutropis multifasciata* occurs in Northeast India, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and parts of the Western Ghats, typically inhabiting low-to-mid elevation forests.
